outcome: placental inflammatory changes (perivillous fibrin depositions, necrosis of syncytiotrophoblast, chronic intervillositis, CD20+ B-cell infiltration)
cohort: The study included 36 pregnant women (33 singleton and 3 twin pregnancies) with a nasopharyngeal RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting between April 2020 and March 2021.
finding: A unique placental signature, characterized by diffuse severe inflammatory changes and SARS-CoV-2 presence, correlates with foetal distress but not with the severity of maternal COVID-19 disease.
